analysis.title: GS Dunn - GS US Daily Download 12 Nov 2026
key_insights: Systematic LS managers were up 1.25% on 11/11 (+2.6 SD move, about 3/4 of funds up, one of the best days since June). Combined with the prior day (+0.9%), it is the best 2-day return in almost 3 years. Up 0.3% MTD.
12m momentum outperformed shorter-term momentum by the most on record for 3m and 6m. The AI/Semis move is spreading into 6m momentum, which is selling off as recent losers rebound.
GS Research expects AI-related hardware and IP spending to exceed $900bn annualized by end-2026 (+$550bn from 2025) and $1.4tn by end-2027 (+$500bn), roughly 4% of US GDP.

GS expects AI investment to add 5.3pp to true 2027 capex growth but only 4.3pp to measured capex growth, and 0.6pp to true GDP growth but only 0.2pp to measured GDP growth. Semiconductor investment is undercounted and imported information processing equipment is netted out of GDP.
GS forecasts 2027 real business fixed investment growth of 8% Q4/Q4, versus consensus of 4.2%, and 2027 real GDP growth of 2.4% Q4/Q4.

Midterm results pose modest risk to AI investment. GS expects newly elected Democratic governors in states with over a third of planned US data centre capacity to impose moratoria on new data centres, mostly affecting projects not yet permitted. Stricter or longer moratoria are a downside risk.

Declining spending on IRA- and CHIPS-subsidized manufacturing facilities cut capex growth by 0.5pp in 2026, and GS expects a 0.4pp drag in 2027, partly offset by equipment spending for factories nearing completion.
Real business fixed investment grew at an 11% annualized rate in 2026 Q1-Q3. AI spending, much of it on imported capital goods, accounted for over half of that growth.

US telecom 3Q26: carriers (T, TMUS, VZ) saw consistent competition and took pricing while cutting device subsidies. GS flags possible seasonally higher promotions and working capital investment in 4Q26. Converged offerings are gaining traction, with fiber net adds improving yoy at T and VZ and TMUS leading FWA net adds.

US cable 3Q26: CMCSA, CHTR and OPTU showed continued broadband pressure. Comcast and Charter announced substantial cost savings in response to share loss and EBITDA declines. CMCSA flagged near-term financial pressure from updated pricing.

Americas Utilities (EEI conference): sentiment was broadly constructive post-election. A potential pause in data center development as guardrails are codified is expected to affect new projects only, and managements have not signaled changes in data center customer demand. GS sees risk to capital plans and rate base/earnings growth skewed to the upside.

GS is incrementally positive on FE, XEL and PEG on stronger nuclear messaging and improving regulatory alignment. Investor meetings were bullish on XEL, AEE, DUK, FE and WEC, debated on SO, AEP, PEG, ED and SRE, and focused on regulatory/policy risk for EIX, PCG, ES, EXC and NEE.

COP: Buy, $156 price target, 18% total return potential. On track for a peer-leading $7bn free cash flow inflection by 2029 at $70/b WTI, with 2027 guidance of lower capital, low single-digit production growth, lower unit costs and 45% of CFO returned to shareholders. Pre-dividend cash flow breakeven is expected to fall to the low-$30s WTI. GS estimates 20-25% FCF per share CAGR through 2030.

Market update: bond market closed for Veterans Day. Equities rose with tech leading. The GS Retail Favourite basket rose 495bps, its third best day in three years. Floor activity was 5 out of 10, with asset managers and hedge funds net buyers on a re-risk across Semis.

Per Callahan, NDX rose about 225bps and is back above its 200-dma and above pre-election levels, with VIX at a 17 handle. SOX is near its own 200-dma. The move is attributed to cleaner positioning, falling vol and the election narrative being digested.

The desk sees relatively little consensus in the market: debate over where the AI/Semi cycle stands and what is priced in, whether this is a bear-market bounce or a new bull market, higher dispersion in software, and a squeezy Internet sector. Positioning and sentiment look like a blank slate into 2027.

earnings_insights: Telco 3Q26 (T/TMUS/VZ) reported: carriers took pricing and reduced device subsidies. Fiber net adds improved yoy at AT&T and Verizon, and T-Mobile led the industry in FWA net adds.

Cable 3Q26 (CMCSA/CHTR/OPTU) reported: continued broadband pressure. Comcast and Charter announced substantial cost savings. CHTR's new go-to-market strategy aims to stabilize or improve ARPU, while CMCSA noted near-term financial pressure from updated pricing.

COP preliminary 2027 guidance (company guidance, not yet reported): lower capital, low single-digit underlying production growth, lower unit costs, and 45% of cash flow from operations returned to shareholders.

tension_points.bear_case: Some read this as a bear market bounce, with debate over what is already priced in for AI and Semis.

tension_points.theme: ai capex and data centre moratoria

tension_points.bear_case: Stricter or longer-lasting moratoria in states with over a third of planned US data centre capacity would pose downside risks to data centre construction spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Moratoria that are stricter or longer-lasting than GS expects.
